## Description

Wald tests and Wald confidence intervals
in R [@RCoreTeam-2026].
Each exported function has an internal version without input checks
that other projects can copy.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `wald` from
[GitHub](https://github.com/ijapesigan/wald) with:

```r
if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("ijapesigan/wald")
```

## Example

```{r}
library(package = "wald")
```

A linear regression model fitted to the `mtcars` data.

```{r}
fit <- stats::lm(
  formula = mpg ~ wt + hp,
  data = datasets::mtcars
)
```

### Tests and Confidence Intervals for Each Parameter

`CIWald()` tests each parameter against `theta`
and gives Wald confidence intervals
from the $t$ distribution (`z = FALSE`)
or the standard normal distribution (`z = TRUE`).

```{r}
CIWald(
  est = stats::coef(object = fit),
  se = sqrt(x = diag(x = stats::vcov(object = fit))),
  theta = 0,
  alpha = c(0.05, 0.01),
  z = FALSE,
  df = stats::df.residual(object = fit)
)
```

With `test = TRUE`, only the tests are returned.

```{r}
CIWald(
  est = stats::coef(object = fit),
  se = sqrt(x = diag(x = stats::vcov(object = fit))),
  z = TRUE,
  test = TRUE
)
```

### Joint Test of the Slopes

`Wald()` tests the null hypothesis that a vector of parameters
equals `theta` (zeros when `theta = NULL`),
from the $\chi^{2}$ distribution.

```{r}
slopes <- c("wt", "hp")
Wald(
  est = stats::coef(object = fit)[slopes],
  var_est = stats::vcov(object = fit)[slopes, slopes],
  theta = NULL
)
```

### Probabilities of Significance Levels

`ProbsofAlpha()` returns the tail probabilities
that define two-sided intervals.

```{r}
ProbsofAlpha(alpha = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001))
```
